worlds.label: Victorian→802,701 continuum
worlds.description: Tourism not rewrite of historical wars; personal exit to civilize Eloi

events.label: Victorian dinner; inventor claims time travel
events.description: At an after-dinner gathering in Victorian London, an eccentric inventor tells his sceptical friends that he has built a machine that can carry a person through the years.

events.label: Model machine demo vanishes
events.description: To prove it, he sends a small model of the machine spinning into the future before their eyes - it simply vanishes, leaving them startled and half convinced.

events.label: Full-size machine departure
events.description: The inventor climbs aboard the full-sized machine that same night, throws the lever, and watches the hands of the world whirl forward as decades flash past.

events.label: War montage tourism through 20th c.
events.description: As he speeds ahead he sees the world outside change: wars come and go, fashion and buildings transform, and war itself never quite leaves the century.

events.label: Nuclear / war devastation stop
events.description: He makes a stop further on and finds the world shattered by a terrible new weapon - cities in ruins and people fleeing underground, so he hurries onward.

events.label: Arrival 802,701
events.description: The machine halts at last in the year 802,701, where he finds a garden world of graceful buildings and gentle, childlike people in fine clothes.

events.label: Eloi idyll; Weena
events.description: The beautiful, idle people of this far future, the Eloi, greet him warmly but seem oddly passive and dim, and a young woman named Weena becomes especially attached to him.

events.label: Ruined libraries; knowledge decay
events.description: He discovers the great libraries empty and crumbling, their books turned to dust - explaining why these people of the future can no longer read or think for themselves.

events.label: Morlocks as subterranean predators/farmers
events.description: Beneath the surface live the Morlocks, pale, apelike creatures who creep out only at night - and it slowly dawns on him that they are the ones who feed and clothe the Eloi, and that the Eloi are the food.

events.label: Weena endangered
events.description: Weena is swept away in a river while the time traveller fights off night creatures, and the Eloi around her simply watch, too placid and hopeless to try to save her.

events.label: Sphinx panels / machine trapped
events.description: When the traveller returns to his machine, he finds it shut inside the great stone Sphinx building by its hidden doors, deliberately trapped - the Morlocks have taken it.

events.label: Fights Morlocks; rescues Weena/Eloi
events.description: Armed with a crowbar and a torch, he fights his way through the underground creatures to rescue Weena and any Eloi he can reach.

events.label: Morlock caves fired
events.description: To hold the creatures back he sets the dry forest where their lairs lie ablaze - a fire that does the Eloi more harm than good when the smoke and flames spread.

events.label: Returns briefly to Victorian era
events.description: After barely escaping the underground fight, the traveller gets his machine back and leaps out of that age, first touching down briefly in his own year of 1899.

events.label: Filby finds wilted flower; understands
events.description: His old friend Filby is the only one left who heard his story; when Filby finds a strange flower in the empty lab - a bloom that belongs to no known age - he finally believes him.

events.label: Takes three books back for Eloi
events.description: Before leaving again, the traveller pockets three small books from his shelf to take with him, the only tools he can offer the simple people of the future.

events.label: Second departure to rebuild Eloi future
events.description: The inventor climbs aboard once more and vanishes again into the future - this time to live among the Eloi and try to teach and rebuild them.

events.label: Open civilizing mission ending
events.description: The film ends with his friends still hoping he will come home, while he presses onward to a far future he means to make kinder - the ending left open.

events.label: Past wars observed not prevented—tourism
events.description: Looking down on the wars of the 20th century, he is a spectator only: the machine shows him history but lets him change nothing of the past he watches.

events.label: Eloi/Morlock as class/evolution allegory
events.description: The film's far future is a warning drawn from Victorian fears: the pampered rich decayed into the helpless Eloi, while the workers they ground down became the savage Morlocks below.

events.label: Machine as stage-magic time vehicle
events.description: The machine works like stage magic: the traveller pulls a lever, the world outside blurs and ages around him, and only a nudge on the lever stops the rush of years.

events.label: No grandfather change attempted; future exploration
events.description: The traveller never tries to alter his own past - the film's only rule is that history he passes through simply happens, and his adventures all lie in the future instead.

ruleEffects.effect: Observer-tourist past; intervention reserved for far future Eloi

outcome.summary: Victorian traveler tours wars to 802,701; battles Morlocks; returns briefly then goes back with books to help Eloi.
